zh.summary: 把確認發現轉成有理由的排序、有負責人的修正與可複查的結果，分清緩解、更新回報與驗證結案。

sourceBody.text: 上一課處理「工具說的問題是否成立」。這一課接著回答：確認問題以後，要先處理哪一個、怎麼改善，以及要拿出什麼證據才能結案？
今天的一句話是：把已確認的發現，轉成有理由的優先順序、有負責人的行動，以及能被複查的結果。
一、用修理房子理解：列出問題，還沒有修好房子
想像房屋檢查列出三個問題：前門鎖壞了、儲藏室窗框生鏽、浴室水龍頭漏水。報告有照片、有編號，也寫了問題很嚴重，但住戶仍要決定先修什麼、誰來修、修之前怎麼降低風險，以及修好後怎麼確認。
資安也是如此。Risk Prioritization 是「風險優先排序」，把有限人力放在最需要先處理的地方。Remediation 是「修正或補救」，採取措施處理問題。Reporting 是「報告」，把證據、決策、進度與限制交代給需要採取行動的人。
房屋比喻有界線：資安環境會持續改變，今天限制了入口，明天設定變更可能又讓入口開放。因此結案後仍要監控，不能把一次通過當成永久保證。
二、排序的核心：為什麼這個問題應該先做？
先以已確認的發現為基礎，再看四件事：

items: 可能造成什麼後果？ 是影響非關鍵測試資料，還是讓重要服務停擺、資料外洩或內容遭竄改？
成立條件在這裡是否存在？ 相關元件有沒有啟用？從哪些位置能到達？需要什麼身分或操作？
目前的威脅情況如何？ 有沒有可靠的實際利用資訊？資訊何時查核？不要把別處發生的利用，直接寫成自己已遭入侵。
現在有哪些防護與限制？ 防護措施是否真的生效？修補是否需要維護時間、相依套件或先做相容性測試？

sourceBody.text: CVSS 是 Common Vulnerability Scoring System，通用弱點評分系統。它能協助溝通技術嚴重度，但基本分數本身不足以代表組織的全部風險。[FIRST 的 CVSS v4.0 使用指南，文件版本 1.2](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/user-guide)明確區分基本嚴重度與風險。本課不重算分數，也不把分數、資產價值和威脅機率隨意相乘成一個看似精準的答案。
修補困難是需要安排資源的限制，並不會讓原本的技術風險自動變低。高風險又難修的問題，可能更需要先做臨時控制並升級決策。
若已有可信證據顯示正在遭入侵，還要啟動事件應變，不能只排進一般修補佇列。保存證據、控制影響與修正弱點可以互相配合，但不是同一件事。
三、處置不只一種，狀態也要分開
修正根本問題。 例如安裝適用更新、修正錯誤權限或替換不再支援的元件。Patch 是「修補程式」，通常是供應商提供的軟體修正。不是每個弱點都能靠更新解決，設定與程式邏輯問題可能需要不同處理。
先降低風險。 Mitigation，緩解，是降低問題造成危害的機會或影響。像暫時關閉受影響功能、限制必要來源、隔離資產。這些措施要驗證效果並記下殘餘風險，也就是措施實施後仍然留下的風險。「入口受限」不能直接改寫成「套件已修補」。
停止使用造成風險的功能或資產。 例如經核准退役無法維護的系統。要確認相關服務、相依關係與資料保留需求，不是看到弱點就直接關機。
接受風險。 由有權限承擔決策的人，在知道影響、替代方案與限制後決定暫時承擔。應有負責人、適用範圍、理由與重新檢視條件。掃描人員不能因為「不好修」就自行把問題勾成接受。
分擔風險後果或管理工作。 例如有契約的保險或委外服務。這不會自動消除弱點，也不代表組織不再需要管理供應商及自身責任。

這些方式可以組合使用，例如先限制入口，再安排永久修正。[NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4，2022 年 4 月，第 2 節](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-40r4.pdf)將風險回應分成接受、降低、移轉與避免；其中降低風險也包含修補。本課把「永久修正」和「暫時緩解」分開說，是為了讓報告狀態更清楚，不是另創官方分類。
四、讓修正可執行：變更前、變更中、變更後
變更前，要確認受影響資產與元件、可信的更新來源、相容性、相依項目和負責人。需要停機時，安排核准的維護時段；準備可用的備份及復原方式，並確定出問題時由誰判斷停止或回復。
Rollback 是「回復到先前狀態」。它能協助處理更新造成的故障，但回復後可能把原本的弱點一起帶回來，所以不能只寫「服務恢復，全部完成」，還要重看資安風險。
變更中，依核准計畫逐步執行並留紀錄。重要系統可能先小範圍驗證，再逐批推進。實際需要的管理權限、重啟或網路設定變更，都要在授權範圍內，不為了趕進度擅自關閉防護。

變更後，至少分開確認兩件事：原問題是否受到預期處理，以及正常服務是否仍能運作。 更新安裝成功的訊息只是其中一項證據；若需要重新啟動才能生效，還要確認實際執行中的元件已使用新版本。[NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4，第 2.3 節](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-40r4.pdf)將部署準備、部署、驗證與後續監控分開，正是為了避免把「有按更新」當成結果。

visual.caption: 圖 1｜修補執行與證據的四個階段
visual.description: 箭頭表示執行與查核順序，不代表每關自動通過；失敗或回復後須重看條件與風險，監控也不因結案而停止。

items.title: 準備部署
items.body: 核對適用修正、可信來源、測試、負責人、維護時段及復原方式。

items.title: 執行變更
items.body: 依核准計畫部署，記錄安裝、重啟及例外；執行不等於驗證完成。

items.title: 驗證實效
items.body: 取得修正已安裝且生效、必要檢查完成及正常服務運作的證據。

items.title: 持續監控
items.body: 追蹤修正是否仍有效、環境是否改變，以及是否需要重新檢視風險。

sourceBody.text: 五、完整合成案例：三個問題，三條處理線
以下是虛構的「小樹訂單服務」，不是任何真實客戶或正式弱點編號，也沒有執行掃描。假設本次已確認三項發現。
A：公開服務的元件有已確認弱點，適用功能已啟用。 它承接重要訂單，另有可信來源指出同類弱點正遭利用。團隊優先處理 A：先評估並核准可行的臨時入口限制，同時測試更新、安排變更與複驗。這是處理優先，不等於不經測試直接更新。
B：隔離測試環境有另一項高嚴重度弱點。 本次已查明沒有真實資料、指定網路控制確實限制可到達性，也沒有已知通往正式環境的相依路徑。在這些假設下，可以排在 A 之後，由測試環境負責人安排修正。若後來發現它能連到正式資料庫，就必須重新排序，不能一直沿用「只是測試機」的標籤。
C：一份報告缺少必要的認證檢查。 這不是已證實安全，也不能憑空給出弱點數。把它另列為檢查缺口，指定補查責任與時間。如果它是重要資產，補齊證據本身也可能很急。未知不應自動排到最後。
假設 A 已完成入口限制，但更新還沒有安裝，報告應寫「已緩解、永久修正待辦」。之後完成更新，但複驗登入失敗，狀態應是「已執行更新、驗證未完成」。直到取得適用版本已生效、必要檢查完成及服務正常的證據，才足以支持這個範圍的修正結案。
這個案例沒有通用的幾小時或幾天期限。期限要依實際契約、政策、適用法規、威脅與系統條件決定，不能把教學案例的安排當成所有組織的規定。

visual.caption: 圖 2｜同一筆發現，分開記錄三項狀態
visual.description: 這是小檢核的合成狀態，不是三個已通過的步驟；入口限制、更新回報與驗證證據不能互相替代。

items.title: 入口限制｜已完成
items.body: 保留限制範圍與有效性證據；不推論套件已修正。

items.title: 更新安裝｜回報成功
items.body: 保存變更回報，仍需確認適用版本已安裝且於執行中生效。

items.title: 必要檢查｜未完成
items.body: 登入失敗留下證據缺口；補查成功紀錄與正常服務結果前，不寫驗證通過。

sourceBody.text: 六、報告要讓管理者能決策，也讓工程師能接手
管理摘要先回答：本次查到什麼重要風險、影響哪些服務、已做什麼、還需要誰決定什麼。不要只貼上紅黃綠數字，也不要把未檢查的資產放進「全部安全」。
技術明細至少保留以下內容：

items: 範圍與條件：資產、元件、時間、來源位置、檢查方法及未完成部分。
發現與證據：唯一識別碼、具體主張、適用條件、必要且已去識別的證據與來源。
優先順序：技術嚴重度、當地情境、排序理由，以及仍不確定的部分。
處理計畫：負責人、措施、目標時間、相依條件、核准或例外紀錄。
結果與複驗：變更紀錄、複驗時間與方法、實際結果、殘餘風險及下次檢視條件。

sourceBody.text: 可以寫：「截至本次查核，A 已完成指定來源的入口限制；受影響套件仍待更新，永久修正尚未結案。」這句話同時交代完成部分與剩餘責任，不必把進度寫成全有或全無。
報告本身可能暴露系統弱點，因此只交給核准的讀者，保留存取限制；不放密碼、金鑰、工作階段憑證或不必要的個資。對外版本應依授權另行去識別，不直接轉寄原始技術報告。
七、怎麼判斷進度真的改善？
數字要先說清楚單位。十台主機各有同一項弱點，可以是「十筆資產上的發現」，也可以是「一種弱點影響十台」，兩種統計回答不同問題，不能混用。同一資產同一問題重複掃到，也不能每次都算全新的問題。
比較前後變化時，要一起看資產範圍、成功檢查比例與例外處理。如果這次少掃了二十台，弱點數下降並不能單獨證明安全改善。
有用的追蹤包括：已確認但尚未處理的高優先項目、超過約定時間的項目、已修正且複驗通過的項目、暫時緩解或接受風險的項目，以及仍未完成檢查的資產。數量之外也要說明主要風險是否下降，避免只追求容易關閉的大量小問題。
「結案」需要清楚的結案原因。修正通過、資產退役、誤報判定、接受風險是不同結果；即使工單系統都標成關閉，報告也要讓讀者辨認。
八、紙上練習與一個小檢核
只用紙筆或本機文字檔，不連任何目標，也不實際改設定。

items: 替案例 A、B、C 各寫出下一個具體動作與負責角色。
為 A 補上「完成入口限制」與「永久修正結案」各需要的證據。
寫一段三句話的管理摘要，分別交代已完成、尚待完成與需要的決策。對沒有證據的部分明寫待確認。

sourceBody.text: 預期得到的是可追蹤的合成處理紀錄，並非真實稽核或測試結果。練習後保留或刪除本機草稿即可，沒有設備需要復原。
小檢核：團隊已限制外部入口，也回報更新安裝成功，但後續掃描因登入失敗而沒有完成必要檢查。這筆發現現在能不能寫「修正完成且驗證通過」？應該如何描述目前狀態，並補哪一類證據？

paragraphs: 不能寫「修正完成且驗證通過」。目前應分開記錄：外部入口限制已完成、更新安裝回報成功，但後續必要檢查因登入失敗尚未完成，因此驗證仍未完成。入口限制與更新回報不能替代複驗結果。
應補上三類證據：適用修正已安裝且於執行中生效的證據、必要檢查成功完成的紀錄，以及正常服務仍能運作的結果。先釐清並依核准流程處理登入問題，再在授權範圍複驗。若只驗證部分資產、功能或入口，結論及剩餘限制也須限定在該範圍，未驗證部分保留待確認。

sourceBody.text: 今天帶走的完整流程是：確認發現，說明排序理由，指派處理，驗證實效，留下報告，再持續追蹤。 報告交出去是溝通完成；風險是否改善，還要看措施與證據。

en.summary: Turn confirmed findings into reasoned priorities, owned actions and reviewable outcomes, distinguishing mitigation, update reports and verified closure.

sourceBody.text: The previous lesson asked whether a tool's finding is valid. This lesson continues: After confirming a problem, what comes first, how should it be addressed, and what evidence supports closure?
The key idea is: Turn confirmed findings into reasoned priorities, actions with accountable owners and results that others can review.
1. A house-repair analogy: listing problems does not repair the house

Imagine a house inspection finds three problems: a broken front-door lock, a rusty storage-room window frame and a leaking bathroom faucet. The report has photographs, identifiers and a statement that the problems are serious. The occupants still need to decide what comes first, who will do it, how to reduce risk before repair and how to confirm the repair afterward.

Security work is similar. Risk Prioritization directs limited effort to the work most in need of attention. Remediation takes action to address a problem. Reporting communicates evidence, decisions, progress and limitations to the people who need to act.

The analogy has a boundary: security environments keep changing. An entry point restricted today may reopen after a configuration change tomorrow. Monitoring therefore continues after closure; passing once is not a permanent guarantee.
2. The priority question: why should this problem come first?
Start with confirmed findings, then examine four things:

items: What could happen? Would the issue affect noncritical test data, stop an important service, disclose data or alter information?
Do the required conditions exist here? Is the relevant component enabled? From which positions is it reachable? What identity or action is required?

What is the current threat situation? Is reliable evidence of actual exploitation available, and when was it checked? Exploitation elsewhere is not evidence that your organization has been compromised.
What protections and constraints exist now? Do the defenses actually work? Does patching require a maintenance window, dependencies or compatibility testing?

sourceBody.text: CVSS stands for Common Vulnerability Scoring System. It helps communicate technical severity, but the Base score alone does not represent all organizational risk. The [FIRST CVSS v4.0 User Guide, document version 1.2](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/user-guide) explicitly distinguishes Base severity from risk. This lesson neither recalculates scores nor arbitrarily multiplies a score, asset value and threat probability to produce a seemingly precise answer.

Difficulty patching is a resource constraint; it does not automatically lower the underlying technical risk. A high-risk issue that is difficult to fix may need interim controls and escalation to decision-makers even more urgently.

Credible evidence of an ongoing compromise also calls for incident response rather than placement only in a routine patch queue. Preserving evidence, containing impact and fixing a weakness can work together, but they are different activities.
3. Several responses are possible, and their states must remain distinct

Fix the underlying problem. Examples include installing an applicable update, correcting permissions or replacing an unsupported component. A patch is usually a software correction supplied by a vendor. Updates do not resolve every weakness: configuration and program-logic problems may need other actions.

Reduce risk in the meantime. Mitigation reduces the likelihood or impact of harm, for example by temporarily disabling an affected feature, restricting allowed sources or isolating an asset. Verify the measures and record residual risk—the risk left after their implementation. “Entry restricted” cannot be rewritten as “package patched.”

Stop using the risky capability or asset. For example, an authorized decision may retire an unmaintainable system. Check its services, dependencies and data-retention requirements; a finding alone is not permission to shut a system down.

Accept the risk. An authorized decision-maker can decide to bear it temporarily after understanding impacts, alternatives and constraints. Record an owner, scope, rationale and review conditions. A scanner operator cannot mark a problem accepted simply because it is hard to fix.

Share consequences or management responsibilities. Contractual insurance or outsourced services are examples. They do not automatically remove the weakness or eliminate the organization's responsibility to manage suppliers and its own obligations.

Responses can be combined: restrict entry first and arrange a permanent fix afterward. [NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4, April 2022, Section 2](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-40r4.pdf) discusses accept, mitigate, transfer and avoid responses; mitigation includes patching. This lesson separates permanent correction from temporary mitigation to clarify report status, not to invent an official classification.
4. Make remediation executable: before, during and after a change

Before the change, identify affected assets and components, trusted update sources, compatibility, dependencies and owners. If downtime is needed, arrange an approved maintenance window. Prepare usable backups and recovery methods, and decide who will call for stopping or rolling back if something goes wrong.

Rollback means returning to an earlier state. It can address failures caused by an update, but it may also restore the original weakness. Do not report “service restored, everything completed” without revisiting security risk.

During the change, follow the approved plan step by step and retain records. Important systems may require a small initial validation followed by staged deployment. Administrative privileges, restarts and network configuration changes must remain within authorization; do not disable defenses just to meet a deadline.

After the change, confirm at least two distinct outcomes: the original problem received the intended treatment, and normal service still works. An installation-success message is only one piece of evidence. If a restart is required for the update to take effect, confirm that the running component is using the new version. [NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4, Section 2.3](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-40r4.pdf) separates preparation, deployment, verification and later monitoring to avoid mistaking an update action for a verified result.

visual.caption: Figure 1 | Four stages of patch execution and evidence
visual.description: Arrows show execution and review order, not an automatic pass. Failure or rollback requires reassessing conditions and risk; monitoring continues after closure.

items.title: Prepare deployment
items.body: Check applicable fixes, trusted sources, testing, owners, maintenance windows and recovery.

items.title: Execute change
items.body: Deploy under the approved plan and record installation, restarts and exceptions. Execution is not completed verification.

items.title: Verify effectiveness
items.body: Obtain evidence that the fix is installed and effective, required checks completed and normal service works.

items.title: Keep monitoring
items.body: Track whether the fix remains effective, conditions change or risk needs review.

sourceBody.text: 5. Complete synthetic case: three issues, three tracks

The following “Sapling Order Service” is fictional. It is not a real customer or official vulnerability identifier, and no scan was performed. Assume three findings have been confirmed for this exercise.

A: a component in a public service has a confirmed weakness, with the affected feature enabled. It handles important orders, and a reliable source reports exploitation of similar weaknesses. The team prioritizes A: assess and approve feasible temporary entry restrictions while testing an update and arranging the change and revalidation. Priority does not mean updating without testing.

B: an isolated test environment has another high-severity weakness. For this exercise, the team has confirmed that it contains no real data, specified network controls limit reachability, and no dependency path to production is known. Under those assumptions, it may follow A, with the test-environment owner scheduling the fix. If a later finding shows access to the production database, reprioritize rather than continuing to rely on the “just a test machine” label.

C: a report lacks required authenticated checks. This is not evidence of safety and supplies no basis for inventing a vulnerability count. Track it separately as an assessment gap, assigning an owner and time to complete it. If the asset is important, obtaining the missing evidence may itself be urgent. Unknowns do not automatically belong at the end of the queue.

Suppose A's entry restrictions are complete but the update is not installed. Report “mitigated; permanent correction pending.” If the update is later completed but revalidation cannot log in, use “update executed; verification incomplete.” Only evidence that the applicable version has taken effect, required checks completed and service works supports remediation closure for that scope.

This case sets no universal deadline in hours or days. Deadlines depend on actual contracts, policy, applicable law, threats and system conditions; the teaching arrangement is not a rule for every organization.

visual.description: These are the small check’s synthetic states, not three passed steps. Entry restriction, update reports and verification evidence cannot substitute for each other.

items.title: Entry restriction | Complete
items.body: Retain scope and effectiveness evidence; do not infer a package fix.

items.title: Update installation | Reported successful
items.body: Keep the change report; still confirm that the applicable version is installed and effective in the running system.

items.title: Required checks | Incomplete
items.body: Authentication failed, leaving a gap. Do not report verification passed without successful checks and normal-service evidence.

sourceBody.text: 6. Reports should support management decisions and engineering handoff

An executive summary should first explain the important risks found, affected services, completed actions and decisions still needed from specific owners. Do not provide only red/yellow/green counts or include unexamined assets in an “all safe” conclusion.
Technical details should retain at least:

items: Scope and conditions: assets, components, time, source position, inspection method and incomplete work.
Findings and evidence: a unique identifier, precise claim, applicability conditions, necessary de-identified evidence and sources.
Priority: technical severity, local context, rationale and remaining uncertainty.
Action plan: owner, measure, target time, dependencies and approval or exception records.
Results and revalidation: change records, revalidation time and method, actual outcomes, residual risk and next review conditions.

sourceBody.text: For example: “As of this check, A's entry restrictions for specified sources are complete; the affected package still needs an update, and permanent remediation remains open.” This states both progress and remaining responsibility without presenting status as all or nothing.

A report can itself reveal system weaknesses. Share it only with approved readers and retain access restrictions. Exclude passwords, keys, session credentials and unnecessary personal information. Prepare any external version under separate authorization and de-identify it; do not simply forward the raw technical report.
7. How do we know that progress is real?

Define the counting unit first. Ten hosts with the same weakness can mean “ten asset-level findings” or “one weakness affecting ten hosts.” These answer different questions and should not be mixed. Repeated detection of the same issue on the same asset is not a new issue every time.

When comparing results, also compare asset scope, the proportion of successful checks and exceptions. If this run examined twenty fewer hosts, a lower finding count alone does not establish improved security.

Useful tracking includes confirmed high-priority issues awaiting action, items overdue under agreed targets, issues fixed and successfully revalidated, temporarily mitigated or accepted risks, and assets still awaiting complete checks. Explain whether the major risks decreased as well as reporting counts; avoid optimizing only for closing many easy, minor issues.

Closure needs a clear reason. A verified fix, asset retirement, a false-positive determination and risk acceptance are different outcomes. A report should preserve those distinctions even if the ticket system labels all of them closed.
8. Tabletop exercise and one small check
Use only paper or a local text file. Connect to no target and change no real configuration.

items: Give cases A, B and C a concrete next action and accountable role.
For A, state the evidence needed separately for “entry restriction complete” and “permanent remediation closed.”
Write a three-sentence executive summary covering completed work, pending work and required decisions. Mark unsupported points unconfirmed.

sourceBody.text: The expected result is a traceable synthetic action record, not a real audit or test result. Keep or delete the local draft afterward; no device needs restoration.

Small check: The team restricted external entry and reported successful update installation, but the follow-up scan failed to authenticate and did not complete required checks. Can this finding now be reported as “remediation complete and verification passed”? How should the current state be described, and which evidence is still needed?

paragraphs: Do not report “remediation complete and verification passed.” Record the states separately: external entry restriction is complete, update installation is reported successful, but required follow-up checks did not complete because authentication failed. Verification therefore remains incomplete. Neither entry restrictions nor an update report substitute for revalidation results.

Obtain three categories of evidence: the applicable fix is installed and effective in the running system; the required checks completed successfully; and normal service continues to work. Investigate and address the authentication issue through the approved process, then revalidate within authorized scope. If only some assets, features or entry points can be verified, limit the conclusion and remaining constraints to that scope and retain the rest as unconfirmed.

sourceBody.text: The full process to retain is: confirm the finding, explain priority, assign action, verify effectiveness, report and keep tracking. Delivering the report completes a communication step; whether risk improved still depends on the measures and evidence.
